tasks.notes: Read the question/reference and relevant pinned-source code; static review only, no repository code executed.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: In _get_response_values, an explicit pos_label is checked against estimator.classes_ for binary or multiclass classifiers. An invalid label raises ValueError; a missing label defaults to classes[-1] only for binary targets, while multiclass None remains unset (sklearn/utils/_response.py:200-228). Separately, average_precision_score requires pos_label=1 for multiclass y_true because it binarizes the labels (sklearn/metrics/_ranking.py:259-268). That metric-specific rule is not a universal multiclass response-resolution policy.

material_errors: Omits requested trade-offs and overstates faster convergence as guaranteed.
tasks.notes: Read the question/reference and relevant pinned-source code; static review only, no repository code executed.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: _posterior_mode uses f_cached only when warm_start is enabled, the cache exists and its shape matches y_train_; otherwise it starts from zeros. It caches the final vector after the Newton loop (sklearn/gaussian_process/_gpc.py:452-495). For nearby hyperparameters that vector may reduce iterations, but speedup is not guaranteed for dissimilar problems. The trade-off is retained O(n_samples) vector state and dependence of initialization on previous evaluations; each evaluation still performs its Newton updates and Cholesky work, rather than reusing a complete likelihood/factorization (lines463-493).

material_errors: Does not answer modification/replacement/drop control flow and implies special drop handling inside composition setter.
tasks.notes: Read the question/reference and relevant pinned-source code; static review only, no repository code executed.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: _BaseHeterogeneousEnsemble.set_params calls super()._set_params("estimators", **params) (sklearn/ensemble/_base.py:251-274). Composition first replaces the whole list if supplied, then replaces a named entry for a plain estimator name, and finally forwards remaining parameters to BaseEstimator (sklearn/utils/metaestimators.py:52-80). A name__parameter key invokes that estimator’s set_params; a name="drop" key simply replaces the tuple value with the sentinel (sklearn/base.py:340-359). There is no special drop branch in _set_params. Ensemble validation subsequently skips drop entries and rejects an all-dropped ensemble (sklearn/ensemble/_base.py:228-249).

tasks.notes: Read the question/reference and relevant pinned-source code; static review only, no repository code executed.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The test fits SelectKBest and GenericUnivariateSelect independently to compare their selected data (sklearn/feature_selection/tests/test_feature_select.py:926-935). Reusing a fitted selector for repeated transforms avoids refitting and recomputing its scores, but transform still requests a support mask (sklearn/feature_selection/_base.py:118-132), and SelectKBest sorts scores each time for ordinary k values (sklearn/feature_selection/_univariate_selection.py:787-801). The source does not establish a measured slowdown or the claimed simple linear complexity; replacing these independent test fits with one object would weaken comparison coverage.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: DummyTransformer increments fit_counter in fit and otherwise passes data through. The regression test fits TransformedTargetRegressor for both check_inverse values and asserts transformer_.fit_counter==1, detecting repeated fit calls on that fitted transformer (sklearn/compose/tests/test_target.py:318-344). checked_claims.claim: Infinity comparison methods are hardcoded and negation returns singleton
checked_claims.reason: __neg__ returns existing NegativeInfinity; even Infinity<=Infinity false.

material_errors: Fails to answer negation and overstates universal consistent ordering across all comparison chains.
tasks.notes: Read the question/reference and relevant pinned-source code; static review only, no repository code executed.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: InfinityType defines __lt__/__le__ as False and __gt__/__ge__ as True; equality tests isinstance(other,self.__class__) and inequality negates that test (sklearn/externals/_packaging/_structures.py:29-52). These are specialized ordering sentinels, not a fully conventional total-order guarantee for arbitrary comparison chains (even same-type <= is False). __neg__ performs no numerical transformation or fresh allocation: it returns the module’s existing NegativeInfinity singleton (lines54-55).
